subject: community-medicine
title: Acarine Vectors: Hard Ticks, Soft Ticks, Trombiculid Mites, and Cyclops

steps.title: Morphological features of hard ticks
steps.tx: Ticks belonging to the family Ixodidae are large blood-sucking acarines possessing a tough chitinous dorsal shield or scutum. As described in **Ixodidae hard tick anatomical features**, the scutum covers the entire dorsal surface in adult males, restricting body expansion during feeding, whereas in females and nymphs the scutum covers only the anterior third, permitting massive abdominal engorgement; their mouthparts or capitulum project anteriorly from the front margin, visible clearly from above.
steps.say: Hard ticks possess a rigid dorsal shield known as a scutum. In females, this shield covers only the front third, allowing their bodies to swell dramatically during blood meals.

points: Capitulum anterior and visible from above

right.title: Female Ixodid hard tick

steps.title: Diseases transmitted by hard ticks
steps.tx: Hard ticks transmit serious bacterial, rickettsial, and viral pathogens to humans through prolonged attachment and salivary secretion. In Karnataka forest tracts, Haemaphysalis spinigera transmits Kyasanur Forest Disease flavivirus from monkeys; Rhipicephalus sanguineus transmits Indian tick typhus caused by Rickettsia conorii, Hyalomma ticks transmit Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, and Ixodes ticks transmit Borrelia burgdorferi causing Lyme disease, classified under **Ixodidae viral and rickettsial vector roles**.
steps.say: Hard ticks transmit Kyasanur Forest Disease, Indian tick typhus, and Lyme disease. Haemaphysalis ticks spread monkey fever in southern Indian forests during firewood collection.

steps.title: Morphology and diseases of soft ticks
steps.tx: Belonging to the family Argasidae, soft ticks lack a rigid dorsal scutum, presenting a leathery, wrinkled, tuberculated integument. Under **Argasidae soft tick morphological characteristics**, their capitulum is located ventrally beneath the anterior overhanging body fold, invisible when viewed from the dorsal aspect; soft ticks live in sandy soil of rodent burrows, feeding rapidly for twenty minutes at night and acting as vectors of endemic tick-borne relapsing fever caused by Borrelia duttoni.
steps.say: Soft ticks lack a hard dorsal shield and have their mouthparts hidden underneath. They hide in dry dirt and bite rapidly at night, transmitting tick-borne relapsing fever.

steps.title: Comparison between hard and soft ticks
steps.tx: Accurate field distinction between acarine vector families is fundamental to vector surveillance under **acarine family differential diagnosis**. While hard ticks attach firmly to hosts for several days to weeks to feed, possess visible eyes on the scutum margin, and lay a single massive batch of eggs before dying, soft ticks feed rapidly within thirty minutes, lack eyes, and lay several small clutches of eggs interspersed with repeated blood feedings.
steps.say: Hard ticks feed for days, have a hard shield, and lay eggs once before dying. Soft ticks hide in dust, bite quickly for minutes, and lay multiple batches of eggs.

rows: Present (complete in male, partial in female)
Ventral and hidden beneath body margin
Slow; takes several days to weeks
Single batch of 1000s of eggs, then dies
Multiple batches laid after repeated meals

steps.title: Trombiculid mites and scrub typhus transmission
steps.tx: Mites belonging to the family Trombiculidae, notably Leptotrombidium deliense, function as vectors of Orientia tsutsugamushi causing scrub typhus. The six-legged larval mite or chigger is the **chigger mite exclusive vector stage**, feeding on lymphatic tissue fluid of wild rodents and rural agricultural labourers; adult and eight-legged nymphal mites are strictly free-living soil predators that do not bite humans, maintaining the rickettsial pathogen through transovarial and transstadial transmission.
steps.say: Scrub typhus is transmitted solely by tiny larval mites called chiggers. While adult mites live freely in soil, the six-legged chigger bites humans, spreading Orientia tsutsugamushi.

steps.title: Clinical manifestations of scrub typhus
steps.tx: Following the painless chigger bite in overgrown scrub terrain, the patient develops a localized vesicular lesion that ulcerates and forms a pathognomonic **scrub typhus black necrotic eschar**, surrounded by regional lymphadenopathy. Systemic dissemination produces acute high-grade remittent fever, severe headache, conjunctival suffusion, generalized macular rash, and potentially fatal multi-organ complications including acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, and myocarditis, responding rapidly to early oral doxycycline therapy.
steps.say: A chigger bite leaves a cigarette-burn black crust called an eschar. Patients develop high fever, headache, and body aches, successfully treated with doxycycline antibiotics.

rows: Black punched-out crust in groin, axilla, waist
Early clinical pointer before laboratory tests
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days

steps.title: Cyclops morphology and parasitic intermediate hosting
steps.tx: Cyclops is a minute freshwater crustacean measuring one to two millimetres, swimming with jerky flicking movements in rural step-wells and stagnant village ponds. As an **aquatic crustacean intermediate host**, it possesses a pear-shaped cephalothorax, a single median cyclopean eye, two pairs of antennae, and forked caudal rami, serving as the obligate intermediate host of Dracunculus medinensis guinea worm and the broad fish tapeworm Diphyllobothrium latum.
steps.say: Cyclops is a tiny freshwater flea with one central eye that lives in village step-wells. It acts as the intermediate host for guinea worm larvae and fish tapeworm.

nodes.label: Guinea worm blisters discharge larvae into water
Cyclops ingests motile L1 rhabditiform larvae
Larvae develop into infective L3 stage in 2 weeks

steps.title: Control of Cyclops and dracunculiasis eradication
steps.tx: Eradication of guinea worm disease from India was accomplished by eliminating step-wells and destroying Cyclops crustaceans under **dracunculiasis chemical and physical vector control**. Physical straining of community drinking water through double-layered cotton cloth or fine nylon mesh filters completely excludes Cyclops, while treating open ponds with chemical temephos Abate at one milligram per litre destroys crustaceans without rendering water toxic for human or livestock consumption.
steps.say: India eradicated guinea worm by converting step-wells into sanitary draw-wells and filtering drinking water through fine cloth. Adding temephos safely kills Cyclops in ponds.

left.title: Physical vector exclusion
points: Filtering water through fine cotton cloth

right.title: Chemical intervention (Temephos)
points: Safe for human consumption; no residual taste

steps.title: DDT pharmacology and environmental persistence
steps.tx: Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon contact insecticide that revolutionized global vector control. Acting as an axon nerve poison under **DDT neurotoxic voltage-gated mechanism**, it holds open sodium channels in insect nerve membranes, producing continuous tremors and rapid paralysis; however, its extreme lipid solubility, environmental persistence exceeding ten years, and bioaccumulation along aquatic food chains have led to global restrictions reserving its use strictly for indoor residual spraying.
steps.say: DDT is an organochlorine insecticide that paralyses insect nerves by jamming open sodium channels. Because it accumulates in food chains, its use is strictly limited to indoor walls.

nodes.label: Contact absorption through insect tarsal cuticle
